# qb Actor Framework (QBAF)

> qb — the qb Actor Framework, **QBAF** — is a C++20-first (optional C++23) actor framework
> for concurrent and distributed C++: share-nothing actors over a non-blocking asynchronous
> I/O runtime with native C++20 coroutines. Two libraries compose — **qb-io** (event loop, TCP/UDP/TLS/QUIC transports,
> protocols, coroutines, time, crypto, compression) and **qb-core** (the actor engine on top
> of it); qb-io is usable standalone. Optional **qbm** modules add HTTP/1.1·2·3 + WebSocket,
> PostgreSQL and Redis. Apache-2.0, CMake ≥ 3.24, Linux · macOS · Windows, x86-64 · ARM64.

Five rules decide whether generated qb code is correct; everything else is detail.

1. **Time is `std::chrono`.** Every timeout / TTL / interval / delay / latency is a
   `qb::duration` (= `std::chrono::nanoseconds`); it accepts finer-or-equal chrono literals
   and rejects bare integers at compile time. `qb::mono_time` is the steady clock,
   `qb::wall_time` the system clock, and subtracting one from the other does not compile.
   Never emit `qb::Timestamp`, `qb::Duration`, `qb::TimePoint`, `to_timestamp(`,
   `to_time_point(` or the header `<qb/system/timestamp.h>`: 3.0 removed all six.
2. **Actors share nothing.** An actor is thread-affine to one `VirtualCore`, processes one
   event at a time, and talks only by events — no mutexes, no shared mutable state, and no
   actor ever constructed outside a worker thread (use `Main::core(i).addActor<T>(...)`,
   `addActor<T>(core, ...)` or `addRefActor<T>(...)`).
3. **`push` / `send` / `broadcast` are `noexcept`.** A throwing event constructor, or an OOM
   growing the pipe, calls `std::terminate()`. Events are relocated with raw `memcpy`, so no
   member may point into its own storage: a by-value `std::string` is never a valid event
   member — use `qb::string<N>` or box it behind a smart pointer. `send<T>()` additionally
   requires a trivially destructible event and is unordered; `push<T>()` is ordered.
4. **A coroutine captures by value before its first `co_await`.** The actor can be destroyed
   while the coroutine is suspended, so after any suspension the only legal channel back is
   the context (`ctx.push_to<E>(...)`, `ctx.id()`, `ctx.time()`). Prefer `Actor::spawn(...)`
   — bound to the actor's cancellation scope — over `Actor::spawn_detached(...)`, and pass
   the lambda **without** a trailing `()`, which would destroy its closure before the
   coroutine starts.
5. **Register every event you handle.** `registerEvent<T>(*this)` inside `onInit()`, which is
   itself a coroutine returning `qb::io::async::task<bool>`; `co_return false` or a throw
   fails creation and yields an invalid `ActorId`.

## Agent reference

- [llms-full.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/llms-full.txt): both agent docs above, concatenated — one fetch, the whole machine-facing surface of this repo.
- [qb — concepts for writing correct code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/llm/qb.llm.md): This file teaches an LLM the mental model and rules needed to emit compilable, correct qb code.
- [QB Core & QB IO — API Reference for LLMs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/llm/qb.llm.api.md): Deterministic public-API reference for the qb-core and qb-io libraries of the qb C++20-first actor framework with optional C++23 support.

## Project

- [qb Actor Framework (QBAF)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/README.md): qb — the qb Actor Framework, QBAF — is a C++20-first framework with optional C++23 support for building concurrent and distributed systems on the actor model.
- [Installation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/INSTALL.md): How to add qb to a project and build it from source.
- [Versioning and compatibility](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/VERSIONING.md): qb follows Semantic Versioning 2.0.0.

## Optional

- [Foundations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/0_foundations/README.md): The layer beneath the event loop: the vocabulary qb adds to the standard library, and the machinery qb-io and qb-core are built out of.
- [ABI, the cache line, and the build fingerprint](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/0_foundations/abi_and_build_fingerprint.md): qb ships as public headers plus a compiled archive, and several of those headers change the layout of public types according to macros the consumer sets.
- [The pipe: qb's one buffer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/0_foundations/buffers.md): qb::allocator::pipe<T> is a single growable allocation with three cursors on it.
- [Concurrency primitives](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/0_foundations/concurrency_primitives.md): The lock-free building blocks under qb/system/lockfree — the SPSC ring buffer, the sharded MPSC ring built on it, an unbounded MPSC queue and a TTAS spinlock — plus the CPU facilities in qb/system/cpu.h they rest on, and the threading contr
- [Containers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/0_foundations/containers.md): The four container families qb adds to the standard library: the node-stable hash map and set the engine holds references into, their flat open-addressing counterparts, the case-insensitive wrappers HTTP headers and query strings use, and q
- [Encoding and conversion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/0_foundations/encoding.md): The three conversions every wire format needs: text to number, host byte order to network byte order, and a unique identifier.
- [The time vocabulary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/0_foundations/time.md): One span type and two instant types, defined once in qb/system/time.h and used by every timeout, deadline, TTL and expiry in qb and its modules — plus the civil calendar types, the UTC codecs, and the single place where the vocabulary is al
- [Introduction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/1_introduction/README.md): The starting point for understanding what qb is, the problems it addresses, and the design principles that shape it.
- [What qb is](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/1_introduction/overview.md): qb is a C++20-first framework with optional C++23 support for building concurrent and distributed systems on the actor model, composed of two libraries: an actor engine (qb-core) layered on a standalone non-blocking asynchronous I/O runtime
- [Design philosophy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/1_introduction/philosophy.md): This page explains the design principles behind qb — share-nothing actor isolation, asynchronous-by-default I/O, a layered and modular architecture, explicit modern C++20/23, and lock-free inter-core messaging — and the rationale for each c
- [Core concepts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/2_core_concepts/README.md): The foundational model behind qb: isolated actors, the events they exchange, the non-blocking I/O loop that drives them, and the threading that runs them in parallel.
- [The actor model in qb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/2_core_concepts/actor_model.md): An actor is an isolated unit of state and behavior that communicates only by passing events; the runtime processes each actor's mailbox one event at a time, so its private state needs no locks.
- [The asynchronous I/O model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/2_core_concepts/async_io.md): How qb runs network and filesystem work without blocking a thread: a single-threaded, libev-backed event loop that dispatches readiness to on() handlers, plus a coroutine layer for code that prefers co_await over callbacks.
- [Concurrency in qb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/2_core_concepts/concurrency.md): qb makes the actor the unit of concurrency: each actor owns its state, runs on exactly one worker thread, and processes its mailbox one event at a time, so application code never reaches for a mutex.
- [The event system](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/2_core_concepts/event_system.md): Events are the only channel through which actors communicate; this page covers how to define them, how the five delivery primitives differ, and what ordering and lifetime guarantees the runtime makes.
- [The threading model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/2_core_concepts/threading_model.md): qb runs one VirtualCore worker thread per engine core, each owning its actors and draining a private lock-free mailbox, so the only genuinely multi-threaded surface is the message-passing layer between cores.
- [qb-io: asynchronous I/O runtime](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/3_qb_io/README.md): qb-io is the C++20 asynchronous I/O runtime under the qb actor framework, with optional C++23 validation: a single-threaded, libev-backed event loop with non-blocking TCP, UDP, SSL/TLS, and QUIC transports, a pluggable protocol layer, nativ
- [The async runtime: the event loop and its turn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/3_qb_io/async_system.md): qb::io::async is one libev-backed event loop per thread.
- [C++20 coroutines](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/3_qb_io/coroutines.md): qb::io::async ships a native C++20/23 coroutine layer — task<T>, awaiters, combinators, channels, structured-concurrency scopes, generators, streams, retry, and cancellation — running directly on the same single-threaded libev loop as the r
- [qb-io feature catalog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/3_qb_io/features.md): An index of every qb-io capability — async engine, coroutines, transports, protocols, TLS, QUIC, crypto, compression, and utilities — with one-line summaries that link to the detail page that owns each topic.
- [What has no coroutine form, and why](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/3_qb_io/gaps.md): qb-io has a full coroutine layer, and most of it is not connected to the network stack.
- [Framing messages with protocols](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/3_qb_io/protocols.md): A protocol is the pluggable framing strategy that turns a continuous byte stream into discrete application messages: it decides where one message ends and hands each complete message to the I/O component's handler.
- [Native QUIC and HTTP/3 transport](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/3_qb_io/quic_transport.md): qb-io exposes QUIC as an optional asynchronous I/O family built on libngtcp2 and OpenSSL: a reactor-driven endpoint owns one UDP socket, hands every datagram to the ngtcp2 backend — which routes it by connection id — and dispatches typed li
- [Secure TCP with SSL/TLS](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/3_qb_io/ssl_transport.md): qb-io layers OpenSSL-backed SSL/TLS over its TCP stack, with secure-by-default client verification, a context-holding listener, and a stream transport that drains OpenSSL's internal buffers.
- [TCP and UDP transports and sockets](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/3_qb_io/transports.md): Transports bind the buffered stream abstractions to concrete sockets, turning a raw tcp::socket or udp::socket into a read/write/buffer unit that the asynchronous I/O layer and protocols build on.
- [qb-io utilities](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/3_qb_io/utilities.md): Beyond sockets and the event loop, qb-io ships a set of batteries — cryptography and JWT, compression, URI parsing, executable-relative resource resolution, synchronous file wrappers, console output and JSON — usable on their own without th
- [qb-core: the actor engine](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/4_qb_core/README.md): qb-core is the actor runtime layered on qb-io, and it is small: one base class, one engine, one address type, one buffer — and one decision that everything else in this section follows from.
- [Writing actors: identity, life, and death](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/4_qb_core/actor.md): A qb::Actor is not an addressable object — it is an entry in one VirtualCore's map, reached only by its ActorId.
- [The engine: qb::Main and VirtualCore](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/4_qb_core/engine.md): qb::Main is a configuration object that becomes N threads, each of them a qb::VirtualCore that owns a disjoint set of actors, drives one qb::io::async::listener loop, and runs the same eight-step pass forever.
- [qb-core features and capabilities](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/4_qb_core/features.md): This page catalogs the capabilities of qb-core — the actor runtime built on qb-io — and links each one to the page that documents it in depth.
- [Inter-actor messaging: the address is the route](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/4_qb_core/messaging.md): An ActorId is {ServiceId, CoreId} packed into 32 bits, and the core half is not metadata — it is the routing decision.
- [Actor patterns](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/4_qb_core/patterns.md): Compose the qb::Actor primitives into recurring designs: finite state machines, service registries, publish/subscribe, request/response with a timeout, supervision, and runtime dependency resolution.
- [Interaction patterns library](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/4_qb_core/patterns_library.md): After reading this you can use the qb-core interaction patterns — request/reply, scatter-gather, discovery, saga, pub/sub, supervision, resilience, streaming, routing, idempotency and aggregation — to compose actor conversations without han
- [Integrating core actors with asynchronous I/O](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/5_core_io_integration/README.md): How qb-core actors use the qb-io event loop to perform network, timer, and file work without blocking their VirtualCore.
- [Asynchronous work inside an actor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/5_core_io_integration/async_in_actors.md): An actor's thread is not its own — it is the VirtualCore, and every other actor on that core is waiting behind it.
- [Case studies: core and I/O integration examples](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/5_core_io_integration/examples/README.md): Five worked analyses of complete applications that combine qb-core actors with qb-io networking, watchers, and deferred work end to end.
- [TCP chat: an annotated walkthrough](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/5_core_io_integration/examples/chat_tcp_analysis.md): A line-by-line reading of the chat_tcp example: how a multi-actor TCP server accepts connections, frames a custom binary protocol, manages per-client sessions, and centralizes chat state, paired with a reconnecting client.
- [Distributed-computing simulation walkthrough](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/5_core_io_integration/examples/distributed_computing_analysis.md): An annotated reading of examples/core/example10_distributed_computing.cpp: five cooperating actor types that generate, schedule, execute, collect, and monitor a stream of simulated computational tasks across multiple cores.
- [File-monitor example: annotated walkthrough](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/5_core_io_integration/examples/file_monitor_analysis.md): A guided reading of examples/core_io/file_monitor, which wraps qb::io::async::directory_watcher inside an actor so file-system attribute changes arrive as ordinary typed events on a VirtualCore.
- [File-processor walkthrough](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isndev/qb/main/readme/5_core_io_integration/examples/file_processor_analysis.md): An annotated reading of examples/core_io/file_processor/: a manager-worker topology that confines blocking file I/O to dedicated worker cores so the rest of the actor system stays responsive.
